answer: Weight each agent by its k-core index in the mutual-trust graph: the deepest shell where every member still keeps k honest ties. A sybil swarm, however dense its own grove of clones, hangs off the real network by only a thin ridge of attack edges, so the cut to the honest core stays shallow and the whole cluster sinks to a low shale shell. Padding more fakes deepens only the swarm buried stratum, never its index against real peers, so flooding earns no weight.
